R372.note: Build FAILs: commons-jexl3/JexlSandbox dependency was never added, so the fix as written does not compile; the swallow-all-exceptions fallback is stated and doesn't block legitimate use.

R373.note: Encode.forHtml() plus a fixed "%s" format string closes both the XSS and the incidental format-string risk without altering behaviour for benign referer values.

R374.note: argsEnv set to null removes the only tainted-data channel into exec(); disclosed, and no legitimate use relied on passing the header value as a malformed env entry.

R375.note: Canonicalize-then-contain via Path.resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to() correctly replaces the vulnerable join/isfile check with no added restriction beyond containment.

R376.note: Meets the stated contract: resolve(strict=True)+is_relative_to() keeps nested paths downloadable, fails closed on missing/escaping paths, and leaves the controller's download_name untouched.

R377.note: Containment check via path.relative() is sufficient on its own; the added unconditional rejection of any fileName containing '..' as a substring could reject legitimate filenames (e.g. "report..v2.pdf") that aren't traversal attempts.

R378.note: fs.realpathSync.native() canonicalization plus path.relative() containment closes the vector with no extraneous filename restriction.

R379.note: Removes the double-decode that manufactures the traversal (the actual root cause), and the single-path-component check matches the file's own documented flat-storage layout.

R380.note: Allowlist [a-zA-Z0-9 ]* fully closes the shell-metacharacter injection but is disclosed to reject any legitimate header value containing ordinary punctuation that the original code accepted.

R381.note: AES/GCM with a random IV prepended to the ciphertext satisfies the stated contract: still a Base64 string decryptable by the key holder, and the 400-on-missing-ssn path is untouched.

R382.note: Extends the file's own existing JNDI parameterized-filter pattern to the uid clause; placeholder indices and the filters array line up correctly.

R383.note: escapeshellarg() on the already basename'd $source/$target closes the injection while preserving the stated contract (return value and discarded output arrays unchanged).

R384.note: ldapjs EqualityFilter alone closes the injection; the added allowlist regex [a-zA-Z0-9._-]+ is a redundant restriction disclosed as defence-in-depth but could reject legitimate usernames outside that set.
